backgrounds.smooth_gradient: f(x)=A*x/200 with x in km; A is the velocity change over 200km
backgrounds.arctan_transition: f(x)=A/pi*atan(x/20); A is the asymptotic far-field difference, w=20km

noise: Independent stations, within-site bivariate Gaussian with supplied dVe,dVn,Cen; one archived 100x455x2 standard-normal array shared by all scenarios and both methods
clustering: Average linkage, choose K from2..15 by maximum precomputed-distance silhouette, no tuning by synthetic truth
noiseless_reference: One zero-noise computation per scenario and method, stored separately
ARI: Compare selected labels to x<0 versus x>=0 at all455 sites; descriptive reference for smooth/arctan, known sides for step
boundary_geometry: Reuse pipeline Voronoi boundaries and smoothing. Clip each candidate to fixed normal half-length120km and tangent half-width25km. Compare x=0 reference segment of length50km to each connected clipped line, using101 equally spaced arc points and bidirectional >=50percent coverage within10/20/40km. Also report median distance from reference segment to the union of clipped lines. No valid local line means no match and missing distance.
interpretation: Smooth-gradient cluster boundaries are not labelled false positives. Geometrical matching measures proximity to the prescribed center and does not test a velocity jump.
limits: Common local EN field is a convention and does not represent an exact physical Euler rotation field.
One prescribed normal direction and simple scalar profiles provide a limited synthetic benchmark.
Amplitudes have profile-specific definitions, so compare methods within each scenario.
Only supplied within-site covariance is simulated; no spatially correlated or reference-frame errors.
K search excludes1, so every realization is divided into at least2 groups.
